statement: Is it true that if $A\subset \mathbb{N}\backslash\{1\}$ is a finite set with $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}<2$ then there is a partition $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $\sum_{n\in A_i}\frac{1}{n}<1$ for $i=1,2$?
status: DISPROVED (LEAN) — erdosproblems.com: 'This has been solved in the negative and the proof verified in Lean.'
notes: RESOLVED IN THE NEGATIVE: formalize the negation, i.e. there exists a finite set A of integers >= 2 with reciprocal sum < 2 that admits no partition into two parts each with reciprocal sum < 1. From the site: This is not true if A is a multiset, for example 2,3,3,5,5,5,5. This is not true in general, as shown by Sándor [Sa97], who observed that the proper divisors of 120 form a counterexample. More generally, Sándor shows that for any n >= 2 there exists a finite set A of integers >= 2 with reciprocal sum < n and no partition into n parts each of which has reciprocal sum < 1. The minimal counterexample is {2,3,4,5,6,7,10,11,13,14,15}, found by Tom Stobart.
